chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ahmad ibn Idris quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Abi Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Hashim, on the authority of Amr ibn Uthman, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Azafer, on the authority of Abi Hamzah al-Thumali, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said:

In Kufa there are cursed mosques and blessed mosques. As for the blessed one, it is the Mosque of Ghuna; by God, its direction of prayer is straight and its soil is pure. A believing man built it, and the world will not pass away until two springs emerge from it, and two gardens will grow there. However, its people are cursed and it is stripped of them. [The other blessed mosques are]: the Mosque of Bani Zafar, the Mosque of Al-Sahla, a mosque in Al-Khmarra, and the Mosque of Ja'fi. It is not their mosque today, and it is said: [it is] ruined. As for the cursed mosques: the Mosque of Thaqif, the Mosque of Al-Ashath, the Mosque of Jarir al-Bajali, the Mosque of Sammak, and a mosque in Al-Khmarra which was built upon the grave of one of the Pharaohs.
ai.seo_question: What are the five blessed and five cursed mosques in Kufa according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* highlights the spiritual geography of Kufa, distinguishing mosques by the piety of their founders and the theological stance of their congregants rather than mere architectural merit. The blessed mosques, such as that of Ghunaym, are linked to enduring divine favor and eventual eschatological reward, while the cursed ones, like those of Thaqif and Al-Ashter, are associated with historical figures whose actions or lineage incurred divine displeasure. This classification reflects the Shia emphasis on the continuity of Imamate authority and the moral character of early Muslim communities in shaping sacred spaces.
